title: Etale internal Hom localization triangle for arbitrary coefficients
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $A$ any commutative ring, and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion with complementary open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]. Use ordinary derived categories of sheaves of modules over the constant sheaves $A_T$ on the small etale sites $T_{\mathrm{et}}$, $T=X,U,Z$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Inverse images $i^*,j^*$ are inverse images of module sheaves, applied to complexes [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. The functor $i_*$ is the exact closed direct image, applied termwise, $Rj_*$ is derived direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], and $Ri^!$ is the right derived functor of $F\mapsto i^*\ker(F\to j_*j^*F)$, where the arrow is the restriction adjunction unit. For every $K\in D^b(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $N\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ there is a natural distinguished triangle [def-weil-triangulated-category]
$$i_*R\mathcal Hom_A(i^*K,Ri^!N)\longrightarrow R\mathcal Hom_A(K,N)\longrightarrow Rj_*R\mathcal Hom_A(j^*K,j^*N)\longrightarrow\bigl(i_*R\mathcal Hom_A(i^*K,Ri^!N)\bigr)[1].$$
The Hom objects are derived internal sheaf Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. The first two arrows are the ones obtained by applying this contravariant internal Hom to the open/closed extension triangle $j_!j^*K\to K\to i_*i^*K\to(j_!j^*K)[1]$, followed by the internal-adjunction identifications for the open and closed immersions. No constructibility, finite Tor amplitude, finiteness of $A$, or dualizing-complex hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Expose XVII, proof of Lemma 7.6.10, displayed distinguished triangle, p. 313 (restricted here to bounded K and bounded-below N).
